title: Single Molecule Fluorescence Microscopy on Planar Supported Bilayers
protocol: Mix 45 mg of POPC and 6.9 mg DGS NTA-Ni in chloroform in a 250 ml round bottom flask.
Evaporate the chloroform using a rotary evaporator without increasing temperature above ambient.
Alternatively, blow off the chloroform inside a chemical hood with inert gas such as nitrogen or argon while rotating the flask to ensure even deposition of lipids.
Attach the flask to vacuum overnight to remove residual chloroform quantitatively.
Mix 49.5 mg POPC and 0.69 mg DGS NTA-Ni in chloroform for a 1% DGS NTA-Ni/99% POPC lipid composition.
Evaporate this mixture using the same procedure as above to remove all chloroform.
Generate small unilamellar vesicles (SUVs) from dried lipids by bath sonication.
Degass PBS.
Suspend the dried lipid mixture with a 250 ml round bottom flask in 10 ml of degassed PBS.
Fill the flask with inert gas such as nitrogen or argon, close it with a stopper and seal the flask with autoclave tape.
Place the sealed flask into a bath sonicator and sonicate the lipid suspension at 120 to 170 W until it turns clear.
Monitor the progress of vesicle formation spectrophotometrically by ensuring that the absorption of undiluted emulsion in comparison to PBS remains constant at 234 nm.
Ensure that the absorption significantly drops at 550 nm due to reduced light scattering via larger particles.
Pellet heavy non-unilamellar vesicles by centrifuging the vesicle suspension at 150,000 x g for 1 hour at 25 °C and then at 288,000 x g for 8 hours at 4 °C.
Filter the supernatant through a syringe filter with a pore diameter of 0.2 µm.
Measure the OD at 234 nm and 550 nm to monitor the clarity of the vesicle preparation and the amount of lipid left.
Store the vesicles at 4 °C under argon or nitrogen.
Pass the lipid suspension several times through a filter with a pore size of 0.1 µm.
Centrifuge the vesicle suspension for 1 hour at 150,000g and 25°C.
Centrifuge the vesicle suspension again for 8 hours at 4°C and 288,000 g.
Treat 24 x 50 mm #1.5 glass slides with a 3:1 mixture of concentrated sulfuric acid and 30% hydrogen peroxide for 30 minutes.
Rinse the treated glass slides under a stream of ddH2O from a squirt bottle.
Place the rinsed glass slides on a Teflon stand to dry for 10 to 30 minutes.
Remove the bottom glass slide of an 8 or 16 well chamber and fill with epoxy glue.
Carefully place a clean, dry glass slide onto the glue-covered chamber bottom.
Allow the glue to harden for about 10 minutes.
Remove excess glue from the chamber bottom.
Pipette 120 µl of a 10-fold PBS-diluted lipid suspension into each well of an 8-well chamber.
Let the bilayer form for 20 min.
Rinse the bilayer twice with 15 ml PBS.
Fill each well all the way with PBS.
Take off 330 µl from each well.
Add 50 µl of cocktail containing His-tagged proteins diluted in PBS to each well.
Incubate at RT for 60 min in the dark.
Rinse each well twice with 15 ml PBS.
Move the excitation beam into the upright position so that it leaves the objective in a 90° angle.
Place the head of the power meter on top of the beam and measure the power of the beam (=P).
Document the result.
Using the periscope, turn the beam into the TIRF position and image an intact homogenous fluorescent bilayer.
To avoid bleaching and CCD signal saturation place a neutral density (ND) filter with an optical density (OD) of 2 to 3 into the excitation light path.
Measure the integrated counts of the entire illuminated field (= Itotal).
Also, measure the size of the illuminated area (= Atotal).
Measure the integrated counts (= ICenter) of the maximally illuminated center spot as well as the size of the spot (= Acenter).
Measure the background signal per pixel (=B) either outside the illuminated area or without sample illumination.
Subtract the background signal from the results measured in 3).
Multiply the number of pixels of the area in question with the background counts per pixel.
Divide the integrated and background-corrected signal of the center spot by the integrated and background-corrected signal of the entire field of illumination.
Determine the size of the spot Acenter in µm².
Divide the camera pixel size in µm by the magnification of the objective.
Take the square of the result as µm² per pixel.
Alternatively, measure the pixel size within the image with a micrometer slide placed on the microscope.
Take the square of the result as area per pixel.
Multiply this value by the number of pixels located within the center spot to arrive at the illuminated spot area.
Divide the power P illuminating the center spot by the size of the center spot Acenter, µm² to calculate the illumination intensity per µm².
Image calibrated fluorescent beads of 0.1µm diameter both in non-TIRF and TIRF modes.
Measure the ratio of bead fluorescence intensities between TIRF and non-TIRF mode.
Calculate power density under TIRF illumination using equation 1: power density TIRF = C • power density non-TIRF, where C is the bead intensity TIRF / bead intensity non-TIRF.
Determine the average signal of individual fluorophores located on a bilayer.
If necessary, bleach all labels on the bilayer in the field of view and allow fluorescence recovery to visualize single fluorophores.
Record images of single molecules in rapid succession using a streaming acquisition protocol.
Monitor the mobility of single molecules over several frames.
Mark the central illumination spot within the bilayer as ROI.
Measure the variance in illumination power density within the ROI, which should be less than 15% ideally.
Determine single molecule and bulk fluorescence only within this ROI.
Integrate the signal of a ROI that is large enough to capture 99% or more of the single emitter’s point spread function.

Take a region of 7 by 7 pixels with the intensity peak located in the center of the square when using a camera with a pixel size of 16-20 µm, an objective with 100-fold magnification and a numerical aperture equal to or larger than 1.45.
Integrate the counts of a neighboring 7 by 7 pixel square that does not contain a fluorescence signal to determine the background.
Subtract the background from the single molecule signal to determine the corrected value for single molecule fluorescence.
Select only signals that are still visible in the following frame.
Repeat step forty-two fifty to several hundred times.
Average the background-corrected signal.
Optional: plot single molecule intensity values as a histogram using suitable plugins of open-source software packages or commercial software.
Experienced users may write their own analysis program in Matlab or similar software packages.
Place a Neutral Density filter of 2 or higher into the excitation path.
Take images of a fluorescent bilayer containing proteins labeled with the same fluorophore.
Record the average pixel intensity within the same ROI used for single molecule intensity measurements.
Record the exposure time of the bulk fluorescence measurements.
Measure the same spot without illumination for background subtraction.
Multiply the background-corrected bulk fluorescence average pixel intensity by the number of pixels per square micron.
Multiply the result by 100 or 1,000 based on the OD of the ND filter used.
Divide it by the average single molecule signal determined in step 3.
Divide the result by the exposure time used in step 2 and the number of fluorophores per protein.
Prepare a fluorescent bilayer.
Place the bilayer on the microscope stage as described above.
Adjust the focus and take an image of the bilayer in TIRF mode.
Apply a short but intense bleach pulse in non-TIRF mode to ablate the fluorescence within a small disk-shaped ROI.
Take an image of the bilayer in low intensity TIRF mode immediately after bleaching.
Monitor the speed of fluorescence recovery by taking images every five to ten seconds.
Move to a different area on the bilayer.
Follow step 2 and step 3.
Take an image in low intensity TIRF mode 5 min after the bleach pulse.
Determine the intensity Ipost_bleach in the bleach area.
Compare Ipost_bleach to the initial intensity I0 at the experiment's start.
Calculate the immobile fraction (IF) using: IF (%) = (I0 - Ipost_bleach) / (I0 - background) * 100.
Determine the background as the measured intensity within the ROI with no excitation light applied.
